title: Endpoint improvement and necessary temporary transition loss differ
problem: Quantify the least temporary objective deterioration needed to escape the strict exchange trap in R27 using single swaps.
failure: A strictly better endpoint does not imply a monotone path or a favorable transition. In the R27 family the necessary temporary E loss tends to zero, but the final gain shrinks faster, making the ratio unbounded.
correction: Define a path bottleneck separately from endpoint gain; exploit count symmetry and prove a crossing lower bound with an attaining path. Verify with exact minimax Dijkstra and threshold connectivity, plus uncompressed identity-graph controls.
transfer: Before recommending a change, distinguish endpoint improvement, allowed moves and temporary deterioration. Evaluate time, costs and persistence separately in any real application; do not transfer the abstract ratio as a financial or organizational forecast.
limits: Specific R27 family, planar equal-trace independent sources, isotropic baseline, single swaps, fixed k. 128 count graphs with 16768 vertices and five identity graphs with 1272 vertices; exact Fraction checks, floating displayed ratios. No general path optimality theorem beyond this family, time/cost model, organizational, physical, novelty or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
